story.head: Who drives the play: the Mammoth
paras: The Mammoth (11-9-3) beat Colorado 4-1 on Wednesday, and the Jets (11-9-3) beat the Islanders 4-3 in overtime on Thursday. This is a Central Division matchup, with the Mammoth fifth (tied for 15th in the NHL) and the Jets sixth (tied for 15th).

The Mammoth have played better than their record (.543) says: their chances are worth about .706, and their goaltending has held them back. The Jets’ record (.543) is about what their chances are worth.

The Mammoth rarely get pinned in their own end (1st), let the point shots come and guard the net (1st) and get more of their shots from in close than almost anyone (3rd). On the other side, the Jets create more chances on the penalty kill than almost anyone (3rd), get their shots through to the net (4th) and rarely ice the puck (5th). The Mammoth are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Jets, and the Mammoth’s forecheck could keep the Jets pinned in their own end.

Clayton Keller (5 G / 24 A / 29 P in 23 GP) leads the Mammoth in scoring and is tied for tenth in the NHL, and Logan Cooley (11 G / 12 A / 23 P in 20 GP) has a team-high eleven goals. Mark Scheifele (7 G / 22 A / 29 P in 23 GP) leads the Jets in scoring and is tied for tenth in the NHL, with eleven points in his last five games. Kyle Connor (18 G / 10 A / 28 P in 23 GP) has a team-high 18 goals, tied for third in the NHL, with nine points in his last five games.
Karel Vejmelka (6-7-2 / .869 SV% in 15 GS) has struggled for Utah so far, but will likely start. Stuart Skinner (7-5-3 / .883 SV% in 16 GS) is in line to start for Winnipeg.

At home, Scott Arniel likes to send Koepke, Barron and Zhilkin out against opponents’ fourth lines, so watch for them against O'Brien, Stenlund and But. One more thing: the Mammoth usually control more of the chances than the Jets do.

items.text: The Mammoth have been without Nate Schmidt, John Marino, Nick Schmaltz and Dylan Guenther for several games. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, only the Avalanche and the Wild are missing more right now.
The Jets are newly without Dylan DeMelo and Isak Rosén.
Gabriel Vilardi has three goals on chances worth about 7.6 goals, well below what his finishing usually turns chances into. If the chances keep coming, so should the goals.
Karel Vejmelka hasn’t won in Winnipeg in his last 5 starts there, and his last win there was in 2021.
